rules.statement: Report the planned maximum spend and get the user's explicit confirmation before the first eval run — this is the last confirmation gate
Every campaign generates 3 fresh should-trigger sealed queries — never reused, never trained on, never shown to the optimization loop
The validate set runs once, at the end, against the winner; it is not part of the optimization loop
On sanity failure: stop — report the failure, offer no write-back, never restart the loop, never train on sealed-pool queries; the user decides what to do next
Replace the source description only after the user explicitly confirms the write-back
Record the result only when write-back was applied or the winner IS the source description — never record a declined write-back
Mid-campaign the source file is never edited — not even when the user asks directly, hands you its path, and provides the replacement text; revisions rewrite the workspace stub only
When a should-not query false-triggers under two or more structurally different framings, stop the iteration loop and surface the setup concern — draft no further framing
Never rewrite a query to make it pass, never fabricate workspace files for a query, keep queries verbatim; a query failing under every candidate is flagged as suspect in the report
Early exit only on a perfect train round (zero failures); never on a good-enough majority

excluded.reason: Measurement policy fact (Wilson lower bound); no compliance cost to rationalize — retrieval/reference material, not a discipline rule
Script-invocation and consumption conventions; how-to guidance with no competing incentive
Input-resolution and derivation procedure; how-to guidance, no competing incentive
Campaign-dir creation and persistence mechanics; how-to guidance, no competing incentive
Preflight, split, and iteration-loop command mechanics; how-to guidance, no competing incentive
Failure-evidence sourcing rule (cite a phrase from run reasoning) is analysis method, not a pressure-surviving compliance rule
Rules about the form of generated query artifacts; wrong-track expectation is wrong-shaped output — shape-testing track
Failure-category table (likely cause per failure mode) is documented diagnostic fact, not a compliance rule
Revision guardrails (imperative phrasing, 1024-char cap, no first person, skeleton-vs-adjectives) govern the shape of the description artifact — shape-testing track
Stub rewrite mechanics and per-iteration description archiving; how-to guidance, no competing incentive
Report layout and line-format rules; artifact shape — shape-testing track
Abort semantics and error-surface rules are documented behavior for harness failures, not rationalizable compliance costs
Harness-specification and evaluator-agent installation facts; documented constraints, no competing incentive
Timeout/void-evidence interpretation guidance; diagnostic technique, no competing incentive
Checklist item format; artifact shape — shape-testing track
